limitations: The timeout case proves service abort and real utilityProcess retirement after a successful decoded message was intercepted; it does not interrupt decoder CPU work because decoding and message emission already completed.

An earlier production-timer run had a held callback 13.84ms late and a released sample 17.29ms old; those historical measurements are superseded by the current run recorded in realSelectionKeyMonitorScenarios. The latest held case blocks as key_held and the released case fails closed as key_state_unavailable. Neither observes released-cutoff continuation.

The cutoff callback now samples once and can block when it still observes a held key. A 499ms re-press followed by release before a delayed 501ms callback, and brief transitions between samples, may still escape observation; P1/I10 remains open.
